name: Fingerroot (Boesenbergia rotunda) extract
short: Few data, two trials by mouth: 160 with dyspepsia, 4 weeks, few adverse events (no counts); 92 people, 12 weeks, no adverse symptoms. Gargle trial: events similar to control.
text: This entry covers fingerroot (Boesenbergia rotunda) rhizome extract taken by mouth. Two trials give by-mouth human safety data: in a 4-week randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial in 160 patients with functional dyspepsia (80 per group; 138 completed), the abstract reports that the extract was well tolerated with few adverse events; it does not give the number or type of events or compare them with placebo. In a 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of effects on the skin, 92 people (the abstract calls them subjects and does not give their ages) were randomly assigned to tablets of a fingerroot ethanol extract containing 8% panduratin A (the abstract uses the synonym Boesenbergia pandurata, which another abstract gives for Boesenbergia rotunda, and does not say which part of the plant was used) or placebo, and none developed adverse symptoms during the study. Other route (mouth gargle, not swallowed as an extract): in a randomized controlled study that enrolled 56 people with head and neck cancer receiving chemoradiotherapy (the abstract does not give the group sizes), lip swelling at week 3 was less frequent with a fingerroot extract gargle than without it (1.8% vs 14.3%), and other adverse events were comparable between groups. Animal data: in rats given a fingerroot extract formulation by mouth for 90 days, there were no deaths, no clinical signs of toxicity and no clinically significant findings at the doses tested (an animal study). No case reports of harm were found. The cited sources give no data on pregnancy or children. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
